prompt: Stage 2-2, level 4, 9 gold, 96 HP. The shop shows a third copy of your 1-cost carry: you own two, so buying it (1 gold) makes a 2-star. Buying leaves 8 gold, and you had hoped to reach 10 for your first interest gold. What do you do?

options.label: Buy it: a 2-star carry wins fights now, and 8 or 9 gold pays the same 0 interest either way
Skip it and hold 9 so you reach 10 next round for 1 interest
Refresh once (2 gold) hoping for a 2-cost, which is stronger than a 1-cost

explanation:
The first rule of the plan is to field the strongest board every round, and a 2-star is the biggest strength jump the early game offers: three copies merge into a unit with roughly 80% more health and damage. It costs 1 gold. Interest is paid per full 10 gold you hold, so 9 and 8 both earn 0: buying costs you nothing today, and next round's income puts you past 10 either way.

Holding 9 gold to reach 10 makes sense only when the buy does not change a fight. This one does. Refreshing is the real leak: 2 gold for a random shop when the shop in front of you already has the best possible buy. Upgrades that are on screen come first; the shop will not offer this copy again next round.
principle: A 2-star on screen beats a gold in the bank. Buy the upgrade, then save with what is left.
commonMistake: Skipping a 1-gold 2-star to protect an interest breakpoint that 8 gold does not even reach.
hint: Compare the interest 8 gold and 9 gold earn, then look at what the third copy does to your board.
